desc:
A BigCommerce store management starter sprint clears the routine work that piles up in your admin. Ecom Swift LLC handles product edits, stock and price updates, order checks and a settings review, then sends a short report of what was done.

## What is a BigCommerce store management sprint?

A management sprint is a fixed round of upkeep in your store. Instead of an open-ended retainer, you hand over a defined amount of routine work, and we complete it and report back. It is a practical way to clear a backlog and see how much ongoing help you really need.

The work is the kind that never feels urgent but always matters: product edits, price changes, new uploads, order checks and a look at what is installed and how it is configured.

## Why store upkeep gets neglected

Running a store means constant small tasks. Prices change at the supplier. A product sells out. A coupon expires but still shows on the banner. A shipping rule no longer matches your carrier. Each task is minor, so each gets postponed, and after a few months the admin is full of stale data.

Stale data shows up for customers. They see wrong prices, unavailable items and old promotions. Orders arrive with problems nobody noticed. Cleaning this up in one focused round is far easier than chasing individual complaints.

## How regular upkeep affects results

A clean catalog is easier to shop and easier for search engines to read. Accurate stock and prices reduce cancellations and awkward emails. Checking recent orders catches patterns early, such as a payment method that keeps failing or a shipping zone that returns errors.

Reviewing apps and settings also helps. Apps you no longer use still add code to your pages, and old rules can still apply discounts you did not intend. Tidying these removes hidden costs. The benefit varies by store, so the report lists what we found and fixed, not a promised gain.

## What a good starter sprint covers

- Product edits such as titles, descriptions, prices, options and images.
- Stock and price updates taken from your own spreadsheet.
- New product uploads with images, categories and options.
- A review of recent orders for failed payments, odd addresses and shipping errors.
- A check of installed apps and what each one does.
- A look at store settings such as tax, shipping and email notices.
- An abandoned cart and coupon check.
- Category and search tidy-up so products are easy to find.
- A written task list for the weeks ahead.
- A monthly care checklist you can reuse.

## How the sprint works

You send the list of tasks and the spreadsheet or supplier file to work from. We confirm what is in scope, then work through the edits in your store and note anything that needs a decision from you instead of guessing.

The Basic package covers a first round of product edits, a stock and price update and an order review. Standard adds more edits, new uploads, an apps and settings review, and a coupon and cart check. Premium goes further with larger volumes, a category and search tidy-up, a shipping and order rules review and a monthly checklist. At the end, you receive a short summary of what was done and what still needs attention.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Send a clean spreadsheet with product codes so edits match the right items.
- List the changes that matter most, so we start there.
- Tell us which products are seasonal or about to change.
- Review the summary and answer the questions it raises.
- Keep a regular rhythm of upkeep after the first round.

**Avoid:**
- Sending several conflicting versions of a price sheet.
- Editing the same products yourself while we work on them.
- Leaving old coupons active after a promotion ends.
- Keeping apps installed that nobody uses.
- Expecting this sprint to cover customer emails, refunds or cancellations.

## Who this is for

This service suits an owner who has not had time to update the catalog for months, a seller who needs a supplier's new price list loaded, and a business deciding whether to hire ongoing help that wants to see the work in practice first. Ongoing monthly management is quoted separately.

## What we need from you

Your store address, the spreadsheet or product list to work from, and a short note on priorities. We never need your password. You add us as a staff user with the permissions the tasks require, and we confirm which areas we will touch before we start.
